title: Great Leather and Cushioning, but Too Tight Across the Instep—Please Offer EE Widths!
body:
I love the soft leather and cushioned insoles, but getting the right fit has been a struggle. Please offer an EE width option! 

 My first pair was the No. 6 roper in size 11D. I could barely get my foot into the boot, and once it was on, it was too tight across the instep. I passed that pair on to my son, who wears the same size but finds them easier to wear. 

 Chisos recommended going up half a size, so I bought the No. 1 in 11.5D. I can get this pair on, but it still puts too much pressure on the top of my foot. There is already a little extra length, so going up to a 12 would make the boots too long. I own several pairs of 11EE boots that fit perfectly—I need more width and room over the instep, not more length. 

 I live in Brazil and have the boots shipped to me, so I can’t try them on in a store before buying. I only discover how they fit when they arrive, and returning them internationally is not practical for me. 

 I hope they loosen up with wear. I’ve considered removing the insoles, but that would sacrifice some of the comfort I love. I would happily buy more pairs, including ostrich and roughout styles, if I could get the right fit. 

 Three stars for now: lovely leather and cushioning, but the fit is disappointing. An EE option would make a big difference.

title: Very satisfying pair of boots
body:

title: Outstanding Craftsmanship, Gorgeous Roughout, and a Small Note on Sizing
body:
As an owner of three pairs of Chisos No. 2 boots—including the brushed brown, an ostrich skin pair, and now this latest addition in the roughout leather—I can confidently say these continue to be my absolute favorite boots in the lineup. 

 The quality and craftsmanship are exceptional from top to bottom. The roughout leather is visually stunning, offering a unique texture and rugged look that easily matches the high bar set by my other pairs. That said, I did notice one distinct difference: this roughout pair feels notably looser on the foot than my other two Number 2s. 

 Do I regret keeping them or not returning them for a half-size down? Absolutely not. While I am still figuring out if the roughout will stretch or behave quite like smooth leather over time, the relaxed fit is entirely manageable and doesn't diminish how much I love wearing them. It is simply a minor consideration for prospective buyers looking at this specific leather option. If you appreciate top-tier bootmaking and comfort, these are still a home run.

I've had my Chisos No. 2s for about a year and the insoles are just as comfortable and supportive as they were when my boots were new. I've bought the insoles for several of my other cowboy boots, new and vintage, that needed some space taken up or that had structural issues.  They make them feel brand new.  

 I bought a pair for my friend who is just now getting into cowboy boots. He was SHOCKED by the level of comfort and support. If I have a criticism, they are so popular that they aren't ready on demand every day.  I need three or four more pairs and my girlfriend needs at least two pairs herself.

title: A Review for High-Instep Cowboys
body:
Howdy. Here’s the BLUF: these are some of the best cowboy boots around, and (not but) if you have a high-instep, consider sizing up or buying Chisos’ thin insoles. DO NOT use boot stretching spray.  

 The long version: these boots are awesome. High quality top to bottom, gorgeous, and tough. I will not buy another brand’s cowboy boots ever again, frankly.  

 …and, I would want anyone with high-insteps who is considering these boots to know that these bad boys may be tight across the vamp/top of your foot. Like really, really, painfully tight (see photo of the red spots on my feet). Admittedly, I have small(er) feet at size 8D on the Brannock paired with a high instep, so it might have been worse for me than you.  

 I didn’t want to size all the way up to size 9D, and the No. 1 doesn’t have 8.5D. I find 9D leaves my feet flopping around in boots, so I did everything I could to make the 8D work—which fit perfectly everywhere else except the vamp. Thus began my boot fitting journey.  

 I tried everything except getting the boots stretched at a cobbler (which I might try first next time, lol). I wore double socks and took breaks; put a base ball in them overnight; put duct tape on my cedar shoe trees to heighten the portion that stretches the vamp. 

 I tried boot stretching spray—WHICH I DO NOT RECOMMEND. I tested the spray on an inconspicuous spot and found that it stripped the dye, so DO NOT USE BOOT SPRAY ON CHISOS. Mkay. But in my desperation I still sprayed it on the inside, which temporarily gave relief.  

 Ultimately, I believe I have stretched the leather as much as it will ever give, and I believe the issue isn’t actually the leather or the last, but the insole. FOR ME, mind you.  

 The stock insole is VERY comfortable, and like a tennis shoe to walk on. It’s amazing. I never had much issue when I was standing and walking. However, when I would sit long enough, I believe the insole would ‘relax’ or expand back to baseline and press my foot into the vamp, causing pain. When I was compressing the insole by standing, I was ok. Not ok when sitting.  

 What finally worked for me was buying TWO sets of Chisos’ thin insoles and stacking them on top of each other (see photo). They molded to my foot well, I don’t have any pain, and the rest of my foot fits well (like before). Now I can’t keep the boots off me! (Yes two insoles are comfy to walk on. Not as comfy as the stock insole, but still). While stacking two thin insoles is probably not an officially suggested solution by Chisos (ha), it worked for me!

title: ISSUES fixed
body:
Had a bit of interesting experience with these. First off, they are beautiful. Truly the best quality pair of boots on the market at this price point. The leather is thick, has a beautiful shine to them, and the shape is just perfect.  

 The first pair I bought, the left boot squeaked pretty loudly right out of the box.  After some research, I found that the reason was because of the metal shank that sits above the inner leather ... unlike cheaper brands they don't use cardboard or foam but rather full leather.  As a result, I had them exchanged. And the process was very simple. They sent me a replacement pair for free.  I received the second and the same thing happened!!!! At first I thought I was crazy but after testing, indeed it continued. After going into the store in person, we realized that it was just the way that my foot shape is, along with how I step. I know this because the actual salesperson in the store wore them and he didn't have the problem. He couldn't replicate it if he tried. All this to say that you have to test the boots in person to make sure that they work for you and leather is very particular. But what I'm really happy with is that they honored the exchange even after I had already worn them and they helped me to fit into another pair. The no 1.. In the future I plan to try them again.. I was in a bit of a rush but since I live a hr away, I'll definitely be going back.

title: My first Chisos
body:
Beautiful boots, outstanding quality, and the customer service is just from a different world! 

 I got my first pair of Chisos last week. I had my eye on them for 2 years, and I was pretty sure I was going to buy No. 1 Magic Black as my first pair of Chisos, but when I saw Brushed Brown in person, I couldn’t resist going with those. The color is just gorgeous! The cowhide leather is top-notch, and the craftsmanship behind the boots is just outstanding. 

 I really love the feeling of these boots on my feet. I’ve got 13 other pairs from different brands in various leathers, but this pair feels very special! 

 Most of my boots are size 9D. A few of them are 9.5D. In the case of Chisos, I chose 10.5D. I don’t think Chisos is off with their sizing, but in some cases, I was wrong about choosing the right size. 

 The only thing I would really appreciate is a bigger spur ledge — to me, the spur ledge is too short and almost nonexistent.

title: Caution, if you buy the number two ostrich skin
body: I bought the chisos, number two ostrich based on YouTube reviews, and there were a few reviews on the website that cautioned about the right boot, not fitting the same as the left.  I chocked those up to variations. In right foot left foot that was not the issue the problem with the right boot and you don’t notice it immediately because the vamp is tight on both boots, but once the left boot is broken in you begin to develop irritation on the right step upon examination of the boot I could see that there’s quite a discrepancy between the stitching on the left and the stitching on the right in that area and so there’s a protrusion of that stitching on your right step that does not go away with breaking. I’ll continue to try to loosen that vamp up to make the boots wearable but the right boot. It’s always going to have that blemish. I’ll add because I wished the reviews that I read about the difference in the left and right boo didn’t mention what to look for so if you buy the boot and try them on if you notice that stitching in the right boot, examine the exterior and look for the area over the right and step and how much further the stitching goes toward the toll of the boot, not a lot but significant compared to the left. Hope this helps because I have $1000 pair of boots that I thought would be incredibly comfortable and that I’ll wear on special occasions when I don’t have to have them on more than an hour or so.

title: Solid
body: Solid. Comfortable. Stylish. Absolutely amazing.

I pulled into a cozy parking lot, walked to the front of the store and felt at home as soon I entered the establishment. It was very close to closing time a quarter to five pm (4:45 pm I was stuck in traffic longer than expected) I was the only guest in the store & was greeted shortly after I walked in by Juan who offered me a cold beverage. I declined as I did not want to waste more of his time because it was so close to closing time. I had done a lot of research on the types of boot styles Chisos offers and made a decision on wanting the Chisos #1 in brown, I also wanted to try on the Chisos #2 for a comparison of comfortability. Juan has a lot of patience. Not only did he give me a detailed explanation of the difference between the two boots, how each color will fit differently between black and brown because of the curing process. He also walked me though each fit, told me what to expect with the “break in” process, Juan also let me try on one black boot and one brown boot at the same time so I can make the best decision for my feet. I need you to stay with me, the next part is a bit much. I also mixed and matched, one brown #1 boot on the left foot, one #1 black boot on the right foot. Then I switched. Next I tried one brown #2 and one black #2, next I tried one #1 on the left and one #2 on the right. Throughout the entire process, Juan was right there telling me how things should feel. I wanted to go with the black #1’s but my right foot didn’t feel comfortable. After that process, I ended up going with the dark brown Chisos # 2. At first I was skeptical about their “sneaker like comfort” but these are the most comfortable boots I have ever put on my feet. I can’t claim this will be the case for everyone, just my personal experience. I would like to publicly thank Juan for his knowledge, experience, and walking me through the process also staying 40 minutes after closing time. I tried to make my decision as quickly as possible. title: Bitten By The Boot Bug
body:
I've recently been bitten by the cowboy boot bug. I already had a good pair of basic light brown boots from another brand that suited me well, even though I didn't wear them often. That changed when I learned about Chisos and found out their HQ is right here in Austin, where I live. 

 I went on a bit of a run: first a pair of amazing python boots, then a very fancy pair of ostrich quill. Finally, I bought my Chisos No. 2s. Simply put, I like the Chisos best of the three. I'm not normally a square toe guy, but the subtle square on the No. 2 is perfect. Something about the look, shape, and design really sets it apart from the other boots I'd just bought. 

 The boots arrived quickly in a sturdy box, and what's inside is what sets Chisos apart. Each boot came in a high-quality fabric bag, along with a classy touch: a handwritten note from an employee thanking me for the purchase and telling me to enjoy them. That personal touch was incredible. 

 When I took them out, they filled my house with the smell of rich leather. The leather is sublime — supple and soft — and the color is beautiful. 

 Now the fit. I wear a 9.5 in all my sneakers, work boots, and other cowboy boots, and I'd call these true to size, if a touch snug. The length is right; the top of the foot and the midfoot are a little tight, but I know they'll break in and the leather will stretch. These feel like the highest quality boots I've ever put on. 

 My only con is the break-in. I haven't worn them every day over the last few weeks, and that leather is strong, so I've been wearing them around the house to speed things up. They also squeak a bit when I walk. I wasn't sure if that was part of the process, but when I reached out, Chisos told me it goes away as the leather settles. 

 I also picked up a belt in the same color to match. I wear a 32 in jeans and bought the 34 belt — it fits perfectly, and the holes are set closer together so you can really dial in the fit. Same excellent leather as the boots. 

 Last was a bootjack, which is a gamechanger if you don't like pulling your boots off the old fashioned way. They slide right off. 

 I absolutely love these boots. You can tell how much thought and care went into them, and between the quality and the customer service, I'd happily own several more pairs.

title: Damn Good Introduction to Western Boots
body:
So I’ve been working in the boot industry off and on since high school, and worn boots my entire adult life via work and casual wear. However, never western boots as I’ve mostly lived in the Rocky’s and in the PNW, so worn logger style boots, combat boots in the military, and lace up casual boots like Red Wings. Chisos is my first western pair of boots, and I’ve gotta say, they’ve hooked me.  

 My general assumption of the current western boot industry was based off of what I’d seen with Justin, Tony Lama’s, Lucchese’s etc. charging absurd amounts for fast fashion boots made with crumby synthetic materials which can’t be rebuilt, reconditioned, or re-lasted well. The idea of a riding boot but with all the build quality corporate profit maximization could offer. Not so with Chisos. 

 These Chisos are built well, plenty of high-quality dairy cow leather which makes them supple but still durable. The hand-dyed leather on my No. 2s has tremendous character, they were day 1 comfortable and have only gotten better after the in-step has conformed to my foot over time. I’ll likely get a second pair soon because I want to beat the ones I have up and keep a pair nice for nights out.  

 Additionally, I bought mine in-person in their Austin, TX location, and would highly recommend this to any who are willing and able. The staff was knowledgeable, kind, and professional. The location was clean and very nice.  

 Thanks Chisos.

title: Overall great looking boot, but with a few build quality issues.
body:
Overall the boot looks great, but upon close inspection, there are a few quality issues with the build. Main issues is one of the boot straps inner stitching was
 off but quite a bit so there is a lot of slack that uncomfortably bends upwards when removing the boot. Even worse was my left boot sole shape in the front was not cut very well and the shape is really odd (almost looks like i'm wearing two right boots) and it sticks out a bit further then the right boot. I figure as with all of my other boots, they will eventually scuff down over  time and will not be as noticeable then they are now with being all new and smooth and shiny. The boot comes with a really thick inner (almost athletic) sole. It is too thick for a cowboy boot and you'll have to size up at least a half size if you want to keep it in. Wish they offered a non cushioned insole version with a standard leather bottom. When I removed the inside, sole, my size I ordered fit properly. However the bottom then was an unfinished rough material so I had to put in a thin dr. scholl type insert to cover that up and for a better feel. All in all, if not looking too closely, the boot though looks nice, however at the 600$ price point, I would have expected a better built boot.

title: Every Man Should Own One Good Hat, One Good Steak Knife, and a Pair of Chisos Black #2s
body:
I bought a pair of Chisos Black #2 boots and now I have questions.
 First question: Why didn't anyone warn me I'd instantly gain the confidence of a Texas oil baron who just closed a cattle deal, won a bass tournament, and ordered a ribeye the size of a hubcap?
 The leather is so rich it looks like it was conditioned with crude oil and Willie Nelson concert tickets. The craftsmanship is ridiculous. I've owned boots that felt like footwear. These feel like a promotion.
 The first day I wore them, my truck somehow gained 15 horsepower, George Strait started playing on the radio without being selected, and three strangers nodded at me with a level of respect usually reserved for astronauts and championship bull riders.
 The Black #2s are smoother than a 1979 Cadillac cruising Main Street on a Friday night. They're tougher than a two-dollar steak and more comfortable than the recliner your granddad refused to replace for 30 years.
 My wife rolled her eyes when I bought them.
 Now she says, "You're wearing those boots again, aren't you?"
 Yes.
 Yes I am.
 Because these aren't boots.
 They're a lifestyle choice.
 A declaration.
 A black-leather monument to freedom, beef, horsepower, and poor financial decisions involving cowboy gear.
 Five stars.

body:

 Do the newly received No. 7 products live up to these quality standards? 
 And I must say, that after a first close visual inspection, everything is manufactured exactly as I expected for this specification. Chapeau!!!!
 For those ordering from afar and concerned about shoe size, I have a tip. Get yourself the Brannock device. 
 It's a device for measuring foot size and can be found cheaply used online. Chisos adheres to these measurements for its sizing!
 Greetings to all shoe lovers!

title: Inner Soles Out .... Damn Comfortable Boots In
body:
I had to wait awhile to get my boots  to get 'Down Under'. Just perhaps the international shipping needs a review. But, I'm here to review boots not USPS. 

 Okay, so I usually take a EE fit. Whilst I would have been a little more at ease with a boot that comes in the wider fit, I watched the Chisos videos, and went with the D as opposed to the next size up (maybe an option for a round or square toe). 

 At first try-on they were tight in the toe box. I started to think these will take some wear in, but not really an option to be frank. I then removed the inner soles (which by the way are some of the best inner soles I've experienced, including aftermarket), and put in some thinner aftermarket inner soles. Wow, that made the difference.  

 I've been a rusted on R. M. Williams wearer for years (its an Australian thing). However, recently I've been somewhat disappointed with the quality. As such, I started to look into alternatives where I came across Chisos reviews. Whilst the proof will be in the 'test of time', so far I am very impressed whilst the boot quality.  

 Overall: quality, comfort, style. Bang!

body:
Been wearing my Chisos way more than I expected I would. I'm able to sneak them into the office even though our dress code is on the stricter side (they just look that clean under slacks). 

 I took the sizing advice and went half a size down from what I normally wear which had me struggling a little bit with them being too narrowt. But, I grabbed a boot stretcher on Amazon and after one session they widened enough to become incredibly comfortable. Not quite on the level of my Red Wings yet but I've had those for about 10 years so it's not exactly a fair comparison. 

 Overall a 10/10 purchase and would buy again but would pick up a stretcher along side them from day one if you've got slightly wider feet--it just makes life easier. The size down advice is spot on because I think they'd be sliding too much otherwise.
